# depth

Imported as `@elffuss/ai/depth`, `@elffuss/ai/depth/sizes`.

## `sdk/depth/index.js`

Depth maps of photos in the browser, with Depth Anything V2 Small (depth-anything, Apache-2.0) on WebGPU or WebAssembly. The model comes from its original Hugging Face repository at the pinned revision, through the Elffuss model store. The depth is relative: 1 is the nearest point of the photo and 0 the farthest; it orders near and far, it does not measure distances.

### `class Depth`

Depth map of a photo. Runs in a Worker; the first `load()` or `run()` asks
the model store for the files of the variant this browser can run (WebGPU
fp16 with shader-f16, WebGPU fp32 without it, WebAssembly q8 without
WebGPU) and checks their hashes.

```js
import { Depth, colorizeDepth, encodeDepthPng16 } from '@elffuss/ai/depth';

const estimator = new Depth({ device: 'auto', onProgress: p => console.log(p.status) });
const { png, width, height, depth, device } = await estimator.run(file);
const pixels = colorizeDepth(depth, ramp);            // ramp: two or more [r, g, b], far first
const precise = await encodeDepthPng16(depth, width, height);
await estimator.dispose();
```

`run(input, { signal, maxSide })` takes a `Blob` or `File`, an `ImageBitmap`
or an `ImageData` (images and canvases are turned into an `ImageBitmap`
first), applies the EXIF orientation, scales photos whose longest side is
above `maxSide` (2048) down to it, and resolves to a `DepthResult`.
`load()`, `run()`, `dispose()`, `.device`, `.dtype` and `.info` come from
`Task` (see core); a failed run replaces the Worker, and the next run loads
the model again from the store without downloading it.

- `.constructor(options)`

### `depth`

Load, run once and dispose: `await depth(file, { device: 'wasm' })`. The
options of the constructor and of `run()` go together in the second argument.

### Type `DepthResult`

```ts
{ png: Blob, width: number, height: number, depth: Float32Array, device: 'webgpu'|'wasm', dtype: string, scaled: boolean, sourceWidth: number, sourceHeight: number }
```

What `run()` gives: `png` is the map in grey at `width` × `height` (lighter is nearer); `depth` holds one value 0-1 per pixel, row by row (1 nearest); `scaled` is true when the photo was larger than `maxSide` and was scaled down first, from `sourceWidth` × `sourceHeight`.

## `sdk/depth/maps.js`

Pure helpers over a depth map: normalise the model's values to 0-1, paint them in grey (lighter is nearer) or along a ramp of colours that the caller passes. No colour is written here: a site reads its ramp from its CSS variables. Depth Anything gives relative depth (larger is nearer), so 1 is the nearest point of the photo and 0 the farthest, not a distance.

### `normalizeDepth(values)`

Scale raw depth values to 0-1: the smallest becomes 0 (farthest), the largest
1 (nearest). Values that are not finite become 0. A flat map gives all zeros.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `values` | `ArrayLike<number>` | raw values, one per pixel |

Returns `{ depth: Float32Array, min: number, max: number }`: the new values and the raw range

### `depthToGrey(depth)`

RGBA pixels of a depth map in grey: 0 is black, 1 is white, alpha opaque.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `depth` | `ArrayLike<number>` | values 0-1 |

Returns `Uint8ClampedArray`.

### `rampColor(stops, t)`

The colour of a ramp at `t` (0-1), interpolated linearly between evenly
spaced stops.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `stops` | `ArrayLike<ArrayLike<number>>` | two or more `[r, g, b]` (0-255), far first |
| `t` | `number` |  |

Returns `[number, number, number]`.

### `RAMP_STEPS`

Entries of the lookup table colorizeDepth builds.

### `colorizeDepth(depth, stops)`

RGBA pixels of a depth map along a ramp of colours: the first stop for the
farthest point (0), the last for the nearest (1). Alpha is opaque.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `depth` | `ArrayLike<number>` | values 0-1 |
| `stops` | `ArrayLike<ArrayLike<number>>` | two or more `[r, g, b]` (0-255), far first |

Returns `Uint8ClampedArray`.

## `sdk/depth/png.js`

A 16-bit greyscale PNG for depth maps. Canvas only writes 8 bits per channel, which leaves 256 levels of depth; the 16-bit file keeps 65,536, enough for 3D tools and for comparing two maps. The writer and the reader are the core's (sdk/core/png.js), which need nothing but CompressionStream.

### `encodeDepthPng16(depth, width, height)`

A 16-bit greyscale PNG of a depth map: 0 becomes 0 and 1 becomes 65535
(lighter is nearer, as in the 8-bit map).

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `depth` | `ArrayLike<number>` | values 0-1, row by row |
| `width` | `number` |  |
| `height` | `number` |  |

Returns `Promise<Blob>`: an `image/png` Blob
